intro: The intercepts kept in the false-bottomed drawer were never logged, and the codebreakers knew better than to ask what else the war had left unrecorded. Each one was pinned to a page of a crossword, as if the compiler had decided every strip of intelligence deserved a home among the clues. At Hut Eight they sorted things the way the pigeonholes demanded: every slip, every return, every loose sheet had its own cut, and a sheet that did not fit was set aside until someone trimmed it. The newcomers learned fast that a pigeonhole takes only what it is cut to take, and that the shape of the hole decides what belongs inside.
echo: Elgar wrote variations on it; the Kriegsmarine typed on it.

puzzles.title: Shark
puzzles.flavor: Everything here has been weighed, not counted.
hints: Standard atomic masses: identify each element, then use its atomic number as a letter position.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with S.

puzzles.title: Cillies
puzzles.flavor: Paint by numbers. The picture is worth exactly one word.
hints: A nonogram (paint-by-numbers). The filled picture is the answer written in 5×5 block letters.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with A.

puzzles.title: Herivel Tip
puzzles.flavor: Only one page of the book survived. Luckily, it was the only page anyone needed.

blocks.text: A drawer at Bletchley Park was found to have a false bottom. Beneath it: a stack of intercepts that were never logged, each one pinned to a different page of a crossword.

hints: Each pair is word.letter into the recovered page (words split on spaces; punctuation ignored).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with T.

puzzles.title: Rodding
puzzles.flavor: Someone on the pier is trying very hard to get your attention.
hints: Flag semaphore: read each figure's arm positions.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with M.

puzzles.title: Enigma Variations
puzzles.flavor: A pub quiz where every answer is a count. Keep a tally, then keep counting.

items: Holes on a full golf course
Continents on a standard world map

hints: Each line is a number from 1 to 26. Turn each number into a letter (A = 1, B = 2, …).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with R.

puzzles.title: The Crib
puzzles.flavor: All the right letters, all in the right words, none in the right places.
hints: Each word of a sentence has had its letters shuffled. Unscramble them; the sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with I.

meta.title: Meta: Hut Eight
meta.flavor: Everything in Hut Eight has a place, and every place is exactly the right size.
hints: Each answer fits exactly one row of the grid by length; the shaded squares, top to bottom, spell the final answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with E.
